Barnston Island is a Fraser River island between Surrey (Port Kells) on the south bank and Pitt Meadows across the main channel; there is no bridge — the only access is the free Barnston Island Ferry across Parson's Channel from 104 Ave in Port Kells, a barge-and-tug provincial inland ferry, capacity 5 vehicles and 50 passengers, running on demand roughly 6:15 a.m.–11:55 p.m. (to 12:55 a.m. weekends), with crossings that can be interrupted by river traffic.
This guide covers Barnston Island's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Condo buildings in Barnston Island

Barnston Island is NOT in the City of Surrey, despite "Surrey" mailing addresses and the "(Surrey)" framing in the candidate-area name. Most of the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A; the southeast portion is Barnston Island Indian Reserve No. 3 (Katzie First Nation). Planning, permits and taxes run through Metro Vancouver / the Province, not Surrey City Hall.

items.t: Barnston Island is a Fraser River island between Surrey (Port Kells) on the south bank and Pitt Meadows across the main channel; there is no bridge — the only access is the free Barnston Island Ferry across Parson's Channel from 104 Ave in Port Kells, a barge-and-tug provincial inland ferry, capacity 5 vehicles and 50 passengers, running on demand roughly 6:15 a.m.–11:55 p.m. (to 12:55 a.m. weekends), with crossings that can be interrupted by river traffic.

The island's main road is its perimeter dike road — the dike rings the island, protects it as low Fraser River floodplain, and doubles as the transportation route; Dyke Road addresses run around it (the SD36 locator test range was 2–328 Dyke Rd).

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere — there is no condo stock on the island in any form. The housing stock is a small number of farmhouses and rural single-detached homes on large farm parcels; Metro Vancouver's study puts the island population at roughly 150 residents, and the island has been farmed since the mid-1800s.
Schools: School District 36 (Surrey) serves the island; island children cross by ferry to their assigned Surrey schools.

Services: none on the island — no shops, recreation facilities or medical facilities; Metro Vancouver's Barnston Island Regional Park provides riverfront rest areas and protects riparian habitat. All services are in Surrey (Port Kells/Fleetwood) or Pitt Meadows, via the ferry.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Barnston Island

items.t: : strata plans in the ALR cause subdivision per ALC Information Bulletin 09 s.6; under Strata Property Act s.239 and Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1), ALR land cannot be stratified in the ordinary course. Combined with the island's agricultural OCP direction, that is why there is no condo product here and none can be assumed as future supply.

Planning authority: Metro Vancouver, not a municipality: The Electoral Area A Official Community Plan (2018) sets the vision of Barnston Island as a thriving agricultural community and expressly does not apply to First Nations Reserves; Metro Vancouver — not a municipality — is the planning authority for the non-reserve lands, and also holds the zoning for Electoral Area A, including a Barnston Island zoning map (Map 12). There are no new developments of scale; the OCP direction is to keep the island agricultural.

ALR housing frame: on ALR land, one principal residence is permitted without an ALC application at a maximum total floor area of 500 m² (no more than 1,000 m² of fill), a secondary suite is permitted only when located within the principal residence, and at most one additional residence is permitted of up to 90 m² on properties 40 ha or less or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha. Exact ALR percentage of the island: Not confirmed — pull the ALC map for a specific parcel before writing an offer.

Farm classification (BC Assessment) — stated in full three-tier form: $2,500 gross annual farm income for an operation of 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha for a larger operation; and $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 ha, with applications due by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" line for farm class is an ERROR — the threshold depends on the operation's size.

Rural property taxes (Province) — the regime that actually applies here: as unincorporated Electoral Area A land, taxes are collected under the provincial rural system (Surveyor of Taxes), with Metro Vancouver and school levies on top — no city tax bill exists. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11 regime as the Province publishes it: rural property tax notice mailed May 31, deadline to pay July 2, a 5% penalty applied to the unpaid balance on July 3, and an additional 5% penalty on November 1. Parcel-specific tax figures: Not verified.

Flood construction: the whole island is low Fraser River floodplain behind a perimeter dike, and Metro Vancouver publishes a Barnston Island Flood Construction Level Study — flood construction levels for a specific parcel are not confirmed until checked against that study. (55+ notes

items.t: Form B diligence (any strata, if one ever surfaces here): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. No strata exists on Barnston Island in any source checked, so no Form B exists to request for an island property — a seller offering "strata documents" for an island parcel is a red flag to verify before anything else.

Fee-simple lots — the default and only documented market form on non-reserve land: a fee-simple farm parcel carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees.

ALR character: the island is predominantly farmland — Metro Vancouver's 2019 study was commissioned precisely because agriculture is the island's land base and economy. Assume ALR until proven otherwise on any parcel; exact ALR coverage (hectares / %) of the island: Not verified. Check a parcel on the ALC maps.

The island's landmarks are the ferry landing, the dike road and Barnston Island Regional Park, not complexes.
Assemblies / proposals, documented as such, never as inventory: there are no new developments of scale — the Electoral Area A OCP direction is to keep the island agricultural.

faq.q: Are there any condos on Barnston Island?
faq.a: No — none in any form. No strata product of any kind was identified on the island; the market stock is freehold farm parcels, plus Katzie IR 3 reserve land that is not market housing, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)).

faq.q: Is Barnston Island part of Surrey?
faq.a: No. It uses Surrey mailing addresses, but the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A, plus the Katzie First Nation's Barnston Island IR No. 3 — services, taxes, building permits and planning run through Metro Vancouver and the Province, not Surrey City Hall.

faq.q: Can I buy a small lot and build a house on Barnston Island?
faq.a: Most of the island is agricultural land under an OCP vision of a farming community; building is tied to farm parcels and ALR rules (one principal residence to 500 m², a suite only inside it, one additional residence of 90 m² at ≤40 ha or 186 m² above 40 ha), so a parcel-by-parcel check with Metro Vancouver and the ALC is essential before assuming a building lot exists.

faq.q: How do residents get on and off the island?
faq.a: Only by the free Barnston Island Ferry from 104 Ave in Port Kells — about 5 minutes across Parson's Channel, on demand within operating hours (roughly 6:15 a.m.–11:55 p.m., to 12:55 a.m. weekends), capacity 5 vehicles and 50 passengers. It does not run all night, and crossings can be interrupted by river traffic — overnight, outside ferry hours, there is no vehicle access.

The Province, under the rural system — rural owners receive their notice from the Surveyor of Taxes and pay the Province, with a July 2 deadline, a 5% penalty on July 3 and a further 5% on November 1 (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11 regime); Metro Vancouver and school levies ride on top.

faq.q: Are there any townhouses on Barnston Island?
faq.a: None verified — 0 strata, 0 fee-simple, and the zero is structural: no strata product of any kind was identified on the island, the market stock is freehold farm parcels plus Katzie IR 3 reserve land that is not market housing, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)). A buyer searching "Barnston Island townhomes" is searching an empty set.

faq.q: What am I actually buying when I buy an "acreage" on the island?
faq.a: A large fee-simple farm parcel with a farmhouse or rural home on it, predominantly ALR ground under an agricultural OCP direction. There is no acreage subdivision, no bare-land strata and no presale acreage product — and reserve parcels (IR 3) are a different tenure entirely and are not fee-simple market housing.

faq.q: Can a suite go in a barn or a detached building?
faq.a: No — under the ALC housing rules a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence. A detached second dwelling is the "additional residence," size-capped and tied to farm use or another permitted use.
